feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear progression, relevant senior-level scope, and a consistent focus on digital communications strategy. It reads professionally and is well targeted, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong subject-matter positioning in digital strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and multimedia for mission-driven/public-sector environments.  
- Writing is generally polished, concise, and credible, with good use of specific platforms and operational scope.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond activity/scope: include growth %, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, team size, budget size, or project outcomes. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than achievements.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain serial comma consistency (“content operations and enterprise web improvement” vs lists elsewhere); “English (Native) French (A2/Learning)” needs separators for readability; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weakens the education section.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent Drupal, analytics, and governance work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and tighten the first sentence for smoother flow.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “enterprise web, email, social, video, and content operations.”
- Add 1–2 high-value differentiators from recent roles, such as Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics infrastructure, or governance/workflow design.
- Consider a rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, email, social, video, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, and editorial workflow design. Known for translating policy and technical issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building scalable systems that strengthen advocacy and organizational communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat heavily across Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and “advocacy messaging” are reinforced in work experience, so keep the intro concise rather than listing too many themes.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform & CMS management • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, insights & reporting • Workflow architecture & automation • Stakeholder alignment • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider replacing “Multi-channel communication” with “Cross-channel communications” for more natural phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” is strong but could be even more specific as “Workflow architecture & automation” if you want to signal operational modernization.
- If space is tight, prioritize recent senior-level strengths over older production-oriented items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while technical tools remain in “Topline Skills” and “Technical + IT.”
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also duplicates “Soft Skills”; shorten to “Stakeholder alignment” or remove.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director entry. Make it feel clearly post-director, consulting-focused, and outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from generic consulting to high-value advisory + build work: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, and cross-channel content operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and emphasize distinct consulting deliverables: AI-enabled search, microsite/storytelling architecture, governance, and technical implementation.
- Add measurable scope/results where possible: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, workflow improvements, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.
- Possible rewrite: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal enhancements, and communications operations; designed modular microsite/toolkit frameworks, improved cross-channel governance and workflows, delivered front-end/CMS solutions for public-facing web properties, and led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy,” “workflows,” “governance,” and “Drupal/web improvement” repeat the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this entry focused on consultant-specific projects.
- Avoid restating ownership of core channels already covered in the Director role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale indicators. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build; compress the generic channel-management bullet.
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize action + scale + result, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- If possible, add measurable outcomes for email/social/video/governance: engagement growth, production savings, faster publishing, improved reporting adoption, or reduced vendor reliance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one strategic, not operational.
- Video/studio language may partially duplicate earlier “weekly video updates/livestreams”; emphasize building enterprise production capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel growth, and editorial operations before you moved into full team/platform leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead line to emphasize scope at that level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Improved workflows” repeats themes already covered in both the Director and Digital Media Manager roles.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to the most recent work: enterprise platforms, governance, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, differentiated language:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy and information architecture
- Consider dropping “audience-focused content planning”; it feels less senior than the rest.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: Drupal modernization, governance, analytics-informed decision-making, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates header/Core Competencies wording closely.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already strongly evidenced in multiple NACo roles; keep only if other skill lines are trimmed.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo work rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented line: Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Drop lower-priority or older/platform-specific items unless job-relevant: remove jQuery first; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if central to target roles.
- Use grouping over listing: lead with strategic execution themes (“CMS modernization,” “automation,” “AI-enabled search”) before named platforms.
- If space allows, align wording to recent experience: “Drupal platform delivery,” “modular content systems,” or “enterprise web improvement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; avoid repeating full platform/tool inventories in both places.
- “CMS modernization” and “Web & CMS administration” already appear elsewhere, so keep only one phrasing here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list that aligns well with the 2022–present leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize business use, decision support, and optimization impact rather than just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity for KPI development, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support” for stronger phrasing.
- Consider changing “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and conversion/performance analysis” if accurate; it’s broader and more current.
- Order by strategic value, not tool type: KPI design → executive reporting → analytics stack → optimization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo Director bullet on analytics infrastructure; keep this section concise and tool-plus-outcome focused.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if they already appear elsewhere in a Technical/IT section.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific, senior-level, and focused on capabilities not already obvious elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: “Video, Studio & Live Event Production”
- Tighten and sharpen the list: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webinar delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Hybrid/virtual event production • Post-production editing”

- Avoid vague phrasing like “studio operations” unless paired with scope or level; “studio system operation” or “broadcast studio management” is clearer

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”
- “Video production and editing” is already strongly evidenced in NACo roles; this skills line should emphasize technical production depth rather than repeat general multimedia language

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent roles are strongly Drupal-centered, this item should either sharpen to platform administration/publishing systems or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms**
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep it platform-only; avoid adding modernization, integrations, or workflow language here since those are already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider deleting one version or making this one narrower.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating generic CMS phrasing without added specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and aligned to the hands-on work shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and keep formatting consistent; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, jQuery | Integrations: APIs, GTM | Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If true, add scope in a parenthetical to signal applied use: “for Drupal/CMS enhancements, tracking implementation, and workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); consider trimming one version.
- jQuery may feel dated unless it reflects current use—keep only if still relevant in recent work.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger, more strategic workflow language elsewhere. Make it more selective and position tools by function and relevance to recent systems work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, higher-signal categories: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider trimming to the most relevant tools for recent roles: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: “workflow automation,” “editorial planning,” or “cross-team coordination systems.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; repeating the same idea here may feel redundant.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are lower-impact than the workflow architecture achievements in recent NACo roles, so avoid overemphasizing them.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the strength of your recent email leadership experience. It should signal scale or functional depth, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Expand slightly to show capability, e.g.: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations, segmentation, automation, and newsletter publishing**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **enterprise/member communications**, **journey orchestration**, or **audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters; avoid repeating “reaching tens of thousands” here unless you replace a weaker experience bullet elsewhere.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications” language in Core Competencies.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and informally supervised a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, name tools/platforms or flagship programs to show substance without repeating later leadership achievements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building/producing rather than leading/optimizing.
- Avoid broad claims about digital strategy or governance here; those are better established in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Consider dropping “organizational” and “contributed to” in favor of stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing, which repeats later digital/media roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries already show progression into operational and strategic leadership.
